clue.text: Woman's endless task was knitting endless clothes

indicators.note: clothes as a verb means dresses or wraps, so the second piece is put around the first
the second endless means the phrase for was knitting also loses its final letter

parts.note: knit can mean join together, as in marriage, so was knitting gives married

indicators.note: endless means the word for task loses its final letter

parts.note: a job is a task

explanation.surface: A woman's never-ending chore was knitting an unending supply of garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's' is the definition plus 's for 'has'. 'clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb wrapping MARRIE around JO; 'knitting' means united, not needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjorie is a female given name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Flyers locally distributed via aficionado touring posh area

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread about into a new order
touring means the fan goes round the letter for posh

parts.note: a fan is an aficionado or enthusiast
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Leaflets handed out locally by a devotee doing the rounds of a smart district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyers' looks like leaflets for distribution, but means birds. 'distributed' shuffles VIA into AVI.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the collective term for the birds of a particular region.

clue.text: Give up doing TV character at the end of spring

definitions.text: character at the end of spring

parts.note: to jack in is to give up or quit, informally
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: Someone quits working in television, a personality at the end of the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; it is the coil a toy figure sits on. 'doing' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a toy figure on a coiled spring that pops out of a box.

clue.text: Most stylish spot to hold last couple of ceremonies the rest were earlier

indicators.note: only the final pair of letters of the ceremonies stays held
the leading letters of the ceremonies go to the front of everything
to hold means the pimple goes around the ceremonies

parts.note: a zit is a spot or pimple
rites are religious ceremonies

explanation.surface: A fashionable venue keeps the last two ceremonies, with the others held beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' is a pimple, not a place. 'last couple of' keeps only the ending of the ceremonies inside; 'the rest were earlier' sends their first three letters to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritziest is the superlative of ritzy, meaning luxurious and elegant, after the Ritz hotels.

clue.text: Book elevated President unknown in general

indicators.note: elevated in a down entry means raised up, so the letters read from the bottom
in means these letters go inside the general's name

parts.note: Lee was the Confederate general in the US Civil War
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A volume raises a President of unknown origin to the rank of general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns the whole assembly upside down in this down entry, not just the President. Ike was Eisenhower's nickname; Lee led the Confederate army.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezekiel is one of the prophetic books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Nears a statue regularly visited in Caribbean resort

indicators.note: regularly visited means calling at every other letter only

explanation.surface: A tourist draws near a monument on regular visits to an island resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas and a popular holiday destination in the West Indies.

clue.text: Laurel providing singular shade from sun

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tan is a skin colour from the sun

explanation.surface: A bay tree gives a single patch of shade from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel' looks like the shrub, but it is Stan Laurel of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan was the first name of the comedian Laurel, partner of Oliver Hardy.

clue.text: Spies ignored military command

parts.note: eyes are spies or private detectives
left means left alone, ignored

explanation.surface: Secret agents disregarded an order from the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes left is a parade-ground order to turn the head leftward in salute.

clue.text: Country rejecting new and old experiment with fanaticism

indicators.note: rejecting means the country's name throws out the two named words

parts.note: New Zealand is the country
the word new is taken out as written
the word and is taken out as written
a try is an attempt or experiment

explanation.surface: A nation turning its back on novelty, preferring old trials, is accused of fanaticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' takes NEW and AND out of NEW ZEALAND, leaving ZEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealotry is extreme, uncompromising devotion to a cause, a synonym for fanaticism.

clue.text: Forty-five cents boy returns

indicators.note: returns means the letters run backwards, coming back the way they went

parts.note: Sid is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad gives back forty-five cents in change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forty-five' looks like a sum of money with the cents, but it is a 45 rpm record. 'returns' turns CSID round.
explanation.definitionFit: A forty-five is a single played at 45 rpm, a kind of gramophone record.

clue.text: Race to compose brief haiku stanzas about king

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the extra letter
to compose the words is to put their letters together in a new order
brief means the word haiku is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A poet rushes to write short Japanese verses about a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a contest but means a people. 'brief' drops the last letter of the poem form before 'compose' shuffles it with the verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Kazakhstanis are the people of Kazakhstan, a race in the loose sense of a nation.

clue.text: Applause both breaking up and confusing composition

indicators.note: breaking up means the letters fall apart and regroup

explanation.surface: Clapping and a split audience greet a baffling musical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabet soup is a jumble of initials or acronyms, a figure for anything muddled, after the pasta-letter broth.

clue.text: Part of multiple delivery to church for carpenter

parts.note: a quin is one of five babies born at one birth
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A parcel split into several deliveries is sent on to a church for the joiner.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Quince is the carpenter among the amateur actors in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Quince is the name of Shakespeare's carpenter, so a literary example of a joiner.

clue.text: Coach and team have long time on ecstasy and crack

indicators.note: on means the long time is placed after the other pieces in this across entry

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a witty remark or quip
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A sports coach and his team have spent ages on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a trainer and 'ecstasy' and 'crack' like drugs; an equipage is a carriage with its horses.
explanation.definitionFit: An equipage is a horse-drawn carriage together with its horses and attendants, a coach plus its team.

clue.text: Ship-builder's son's old-style jests capturing hearts

indicators.note: capturing means the jests surround the card suit letter

parts.note: japeth is the archaic -eth form of japes, jokes or jests
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A shipwright's boy cracks jokes that win people's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship-builder is Noah, builder of the ark; the possessive belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Japheth was one of the three sons of Noah, who built the ark.

clue.text: Just half spike needed to secure kilometre post to ditch

indicators.note: half means only the front half of the word is used
needed to secure means the spike holds the distance letters

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: A fence post needs only half a spike to fix it a kilometre from the ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a fence post, but it is mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk mail is unwanted advertising that arrives in the letterbox, fit only for throwing away.

clue.text: Hollow fitting round a series of taps

parts.note: a pit is a hollow in the ground

indicators.note: round means the word for fitting goes around the letter a

parts.note: apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: A recess is fitted around a run of water taps.
explanation.definitionFit: Pit-a-pat imitates a quick succession of light taps, like rain or a racing heart.

clue.text: The rain lashed western plain

indicators.note: lashed means beaten wildly, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Rain beat down on the prairie out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like a prairie, but means unadorned. 'lashed' rearranges THE RAIN into INTHERA.
explanation.definitionFit: In the raw means naked or crude, in its natural unrefined state, so bare or simple.

clue.text: A torch-bearer conserving energy with a type of juice

indicators.note: conserving means keeping the energy letter inside

parts.note: to carry a torch for someone is to love them unrequitedly
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An Olympic flame carrier saves energy with a sports drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torch-bearer' looks Olympic, but one who carries a torch for someone is a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera juice comes from the gel of the succulent plant of the same name.

clue.text: Granny with little boy one's impolitely asked to get

parts.note: a granny is a type of knot
Ted is a short form of Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A grandmother with her small grandson gets told rudely where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get knotted' is a rude British brush-off, like 'get lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom get knotted, a rude dismissal, completes the phrase the definition describes.

clue.text: Burnt splinters have dark colour

indicators.note: splinters as a verb means breaks into pieces, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Charred slivers of wood take on a deep shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splinters' looks like a noun after 'Burnt', but it is a verb rearranging that word into NUTBR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut-brown is the deep brown of a ripe hazelnut, a dark shade.

clue.text: Go round chasing groups in banks, perhaps, wielding blade

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the circling word comes after the blood groups

parts.note: O and A are blood groups, the kind stored in blood banks
to ring something is to go round it, encircle it

explanation.surface: Someone circles a bank's teams of staff, wielding a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests money or rivers, but these are blood banks holding groups O and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaring means rowing, working the oar whose flat end is called the blade.

clue.text: Male doctor stops disease in common people

indicators.note: stops means plugs the gap, so these letters sit inside the disease

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis
he is the male pronoun
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A male physician halts an epidemic among ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: TB stands for tuberculosis and MO for Medical Officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The mob is a disparaging name for the masses, the ordinary populace.

clue.text: Film family, hearing notices, fusses about run

indicators.note: hearing means the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to mark something is to notice it, so marks are notices

indicators.note: about means the fusses go round the cricket letter

parts.note: bothers are fusses or troubles
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A household, hearing the notices posted, makes a fuss about a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' works only on the notices, which sound like the comedians' surname; R is the cricket abbreviation for run.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho, Chico, Harpo and Zeppo were the comedy siblings of 1930s Hollywood films.

clue.text: Queen following pages catches one repeating phrase

indicators.note: catches means the letters close around the numeral

parts.note: R is short for Regina, queen
ff. is the abbreviation for following pages
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monarch, reading on through the pages, finds one passage repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' seems to say the queen comes after the pages, but 'following pages' is FF.
explanation.definitionFit: A riff is a short repeated musical phrase, as in rock or jazz.

clue.text: Steers round then reverses not quite far enough

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O

indicators.note: reverses means the remaining letters run backwards
falling a little short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: next means then, after that

explanation.surface: A driver steers around a bend, then backs up but not quite far enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steers' looks like a verb about driving, but it is the noun for castrated bullocks. 'not quite far enough' drops the T of NEXT, and 'reverses' turns NEX into XEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Steers are young castrated male cattle, the same animals as oxen.

clue.text: Encroach on popular form of theatre

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the fringe is alternative or experimental theatre, as at the Edinburgh Festival

explanation.surface: Mainstream fare is muscling in on alternative theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fringe is the umbrella name for alternative theatre outside the main festival programme, as in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe is to trespass on someone's rights or territory, a synonym of encroaching upon them.

clue.text: Avoid promotion, losing game

parts.note: a side that is down is behind or losing
a play is a game or bout of sport

explanation.surface: A footballer dodges going up a division by losing a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' suggests a league table, but here it means publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to minimise it rather than publicise or talk it up.
